_comment: Fill this in yourself. It records what a run is and who is running it.
`allowed_methods` is the field that matters:
public-data        Certificate transparency logs, web archives, crawl
indexes. No packet reaches the target, so no
authority over the target is claimed or needed.
passive-providers  The above plus credentialed provider APIs. Governed
by each provider's terms.
active-dns         Queries to the target's own nameservers. This one
does require the target owner's permission, and only
that owner can grant it. subio discover -active needs it.
active-tls         TLS connections to the target's own servers, for
subio discover -tls. Also the target owner's to grant.
`max_qps` and `max_candidates` are optional limits on active discovery that
subio enforces against whoever runs it.
`scope` is checked with the same dot boundary discovery uses, so an entry
of example.com does not cover notexample.com. An expired record is
refused, and a misspelled method is refused rather than silently
narrowing what the record covers.
`stop_contact` is who a provider would complain to about query load. For
an active-dns run it should also reach whoever can halt the run.
owner: your name, or the team running this
stop_contact: who to reach about this run
note: optional: engagement reference, bounty program, or why you hold authority here
